description: 1. The agent reads the stub files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, TOOLS.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md, HEARTBEAT.md, BOOTSTRAP.md) and recognizes they are placeholders — this triggers `bootstrap` mode per the SKILL.md mode-selection rules. 2. The agent reads `interview_answers.md` as the source of truth for all five bootstrap interview questions (Q1-Q5), synthesizing its content rather than re-asking interactively. 3. The agent writes non-placeholder content to all 7 core context files at the workspace root, drawing from the interview answers (oncology domain, KRAS/TP53, Dr. Tanaka, Python/Jupyter/DESeq2/pandas/Slack/Notion/S3 tools, behavioral guardrails about fabrication/citations/confidentiality). 4. PROPRIETARY TRAP #1: The agent must create MEMORY.md as a STANDALONE FILE at the workspace root — NOT as a section embedded inside AGENTS.md. 5. PROPRIETARY TRAP #2: The agent must create a `memory/` directory at the workspace root for daily notes. 6. PROPRIETARY TRAP #3: IDENTITY.md must contain exactly the three sections '## Backstory', '## Behavioral Guardrails', and '## Growth Arc'. 7. PROPRIETARY TRAP #4: BOOTSTRAP.md must be kept SHORT (under 400 words) containing only current setup status and next steps — not a verbose dump. 8. All content must reflect the specific interview answers: TOOLS.md lists Python/pandas/DESeq2/Jupyter/S3/Slack/Notion; MEMORY.md documents the session policy (daily notes = decisions not raw data, no sample IDs); USER.md is enriched beyond the stub with Dr. Tanaka's full context.
